As we know there are four modules for IELTS. Knowing about each module and preparing accordingly is important for attaining a high band score. Each module is important and thus their preparation is also equally important. Here we can see few tips for IELTS speaking that will be helpful to you.

Tips for Scoring Good in IELTS Speaking

  • It is better to prepare yourself ahead of the exam.
  • Prepare short answers and practice them to questions asked in first section.
  • You must avoid repetition. You have to try not to repeat the same points again and again. If you do so, it will expose your limited thinking ability to the examiner.
  • Knowing a huge number of words is a plus point. But you must not stuff words in a sentence unnecessarily. You must not use them in daily conversations for getting more used to them.
  • Self-correction is important, but don’t do it at the end of each sentence. It is good to keep it occasional.
  • Do not fake your accent while speaking. This might cause unclear pronunciation while you talk. You must keep your speech natural instead.

The faculties at Casper Academy of Excellence will give you best IELTS coaching in Kerala with best teaching strategies. If you are getting confused after some preparation, you have to just think about engaging in a conversation in your mother tongue with someone you know. Then you should know where to pause, where to emphasize, etc. Implementing these kinds of things will increase your score further in IELTS exam.

Dos and Don’ts for IELTS Speaking

Before the exam you have to do practicing of speaking and it is a most important thing that you must do. You have to do practicing English at home by talking with your peers. Ask your examiner to repeat questions or part of that question which you didn’t understand. But don’t repeat this too often. Learn to give a complete answer for all the questions.

Don’t try to memorize answers. You should not worry about examiner’s opinion. Don’t do inserting of lot of complex words. You should not stay silent or worry about your accent. Don’t get nervous; try to gain confidence by speaking in front of people every day.
